The *Sīhaṅgapañha* ("The Lion", Mil 7.6.1) is a text situated within the seventh book of the *Milindapañha* [SuttaCentral]. The text draws upon the qualities or attributes of a lion as a simile for ascetic practice and the spiritual qualities of a practitioner [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records three translations across three modern languages, and notes a thematic or textual connection to the *Santuṭṭhasutta* (SN 16.1) of the *Saṃyutta Nikāya* [SuttaCentral].
Computational text-reuse data from DharmaNexus reflects the repetitive, formulaic nature of Book 7 of the *Milindapañha*, identifying 624 matching passages across 56 Pali works [DharmaNexus]. Its closest internal alignments are with other simile-based chapters of the *Milindapañha*, including the *Ākāsaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.4.6), *Sūriyaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.4.8), *Meghaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.7.6), and *Pabbataṅgapañha* (Mil 7.4.5) [DharmaNexus]. In agreement with SuttaCentral's cross-reference to SN 16.1, DharmaNexus identifies a substantial near-identical passage shared between Mil 7.6.1 (§8.1) and the *Kassapa Saṃyutta* (SN 16) with 97% similarity, as well as reuse with the *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 16) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, DharmaNexus identifies machine alignments with the Chinese *Ekottarika Āgama* (T 125), the Tibetan *Ārya-kuśalamūlaparidharana-mahāyānasūtra* (D0101), and a Tibetan Śrāmaṇera commentary (D4125) [DharmaNexus].
